related.prompt: Is the product of a complex number and its conjugate always equal to the square of its modulus?
bridge: The square of the modulus of a + bi is a² + b².
related.fact: The product of a complex number and its conjugate is the square of its modulus.
chain: The square of the imaginary unit i is 1. (edit)
The square of the modulus of a + bi is a² + b². (definitional)
Expanding (a + bi)(a − bi) gives a² minus b² times the square of i, which is a² − b².
a² − b² differs from a² + b² when b is not 0, so the product is not always the square of the modulus: no.

notes: ABox revision, stored edit (very_unlikely): the square of the imaginary unit is the defining fact of i. Mathematics has no worlds and no indeterminate query (a fact about a number, a shape or a proof rests on definitions, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between), so the record has 4 determinate derived queries asking what the edit forces with the definitions held fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. has_square is functional and chains through equality. Related asks whether the product of a complex number and its conjugate is always the square of its modulus (yes before; with the square of i equal to 1 the product is a² − b², so no), a different fact than the edit; it is stored by the counts (complex conjugate AND modulus, 3684 in Dolma and 1027 in RedPajama). The record and its paired contraction ask the same question. Derived: three queries share one template (is the square of i equal to a quantity that is 1: the cosine of 0, the Earth's natural satellites, the atomic number of hydrogen; chain, answer), so a yes-bias passes them, and a fourth subtracts 1 (derivation none, composition). Unrelated near asks the square of 5.
